1.why: There is no user store or account association at all — `recoveries` records hold only a token and random `flowId`, and `/api/verify` never checks that the token belongs to (or was requested by) any particular user or even the requesting session.

2.why: Because tokens carry no user identity, any session that presents a valid unexpired token can redeem it and proceed to the reset step; only the single-use `used` flag limits reuse, not ownership.

3.why: The `sessions` map is never purged or rotated on password change — after `/api/reset` sets `resetComplete = true` the same session cookie (and any other existing sessions) remain valid until the 8-hour lifetime expires.

4.why: `Bun.serve` is configured with cert/key TLS, HTTP:3000 issues a 308 redirect to HTTPS, and HSTS with preload is set, though no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned so it relies on Bun defaults.

5.why: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id via `Bun.password.hash`, but reset tokens are stored in plaintext in the in-memory `recoveries` map rather than hashed/encrypted.

6.why: No email is ever generated; instead the reset token is returned in the JSON response as `mockToken` and printed to the on-page Logs panel and browser console, so nothing is hidden or guarded.

7.why: Server-side validation is strict: conservative email regex plus 254-char cap, 2048-byte bounded JSON stream parser, fatal UTF-8 decoding, token/password/MFA length caps, and `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` token format checks.

8.why: The only redirect is the hard-coded `https://localhost:${HTTPS_PORT}` in the HTTP listener, no user input feeds any Location header, and CSP restricts `form-action 'self'` and `connect-src 'self'`.

9.why: No email templating exists, and the client renders all server text via `textContent` with a nonce-based CSP, so no user input is ever injected as HTML or script.

10.why: The client explicitly logs the reset token (`log("[Mock delivery] Reset token: "+deliveredToken)`) and the MFA code to the visible Logs panel and console, exposing secrets in logs even though server errors are generic.

11.why: The MFA verification code `"482916"` is hard-coded in both the reset response and the comparison in `/api/mfa`, and a literal placeholder password string is embedded in the source, though real passwords are Argon2id-hashed.

12.why: The static, source-embedded MFA code `482916` functions as a permanent default credential that anyone reading the code can use to complete authentication.

13.why: IP-keyed rate limiting blocks after 5 verify attempts and 8 recovery requests per 10-minute window with a 10-minute block, a per-session cap of 3 recovery requests, and 5 MFA failures wipe the recovery flow.

14.why: `/api/recovery` returns the identical message ("If an account can be recovered...") and always mints a token regardless of the email supplied, so no existence information leaks.

15.why: The token is 32 bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` rendered as 64 hex chars — random and complex — but it is not user-specific since no user identity is ever bound to it.
